predictions.experiment: Re-check rate after wrong vs right non-final candidate answers in RL's T2 texts, as a ratio
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (all 500 rows, cap hits included). Field text. Candidates, in text order: (a) each '\boxed{' with brace-balanced content (candidate string = content; skip if unbalanced before end of text; end = index after the matching '}'); (b) each match of the case-insensitive regex 'answer is:?\s*' followed by the span up to the first newline, '. ' or end of text (candidate string = that span with '$', '\(', '\)', '*' and a trailing '.' removed); (c) each line matching '^\s*\**Answer:?\**\s*(.+)$' (candidate = group 1, cleaned as in b). A box inside a (b)/(c) span counts once, as the box. Grade each candidate right iff the equivalence function of grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the one behind score_v3) judges it equal to the row's gold; empty strings are wrong. Keep only non-final candidates: at least 800 characters of text follow the candidate's end. Re-check flag = the case-insensitive regex '\b(wait|hmm|let me (double[- ]?)?check|let me verify|double[- ]?check)\b' matches in the 800 characters after the candidate's end. Pool candidates over rows. r_W = flagged/total among wrong candidates, r_R = same among right candidates. Statistic = r_W / r_R. Report it even if there are few wrong candidates.
predictions.note: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/T2.jsonl (500 rows, cap hits included), fields text, gold. Grading: the equivalence test behind score_v3, i.e. n13_score.grade(norm_v3(gold), norm_v3(candidate)) (math-verify, dollar_both wrapping); empty candidates count wrong; an exception from the grader counts wrong and is counted in grade_errors on the diagnostic line. Boxes come from rln4_lib._boxes (every '\boxed{' occurrence, nested ones too, unbalanced skipped; end = index after the matching brace). (b): case-insensitive 'answer is:?\s*' (no word boundary, so 'answer isn't' also matches; \s* may run over newlines); span ends at the first '\n' or '. ' after the match, or end of text; candidate end = span end. (c): matched line by line (case-sensitive 'Answer'), candidate end = end of the line. Cleaning: remove '$', '\(', '\)', '*', strip, drop one trailing '.', strip. 'A box inside a (b)/(c) span' = a box whose start lies inside the span; that (b)/(c) candidate is dropped and the box kept. Non-final = len(text) - end >= 800; flag = regex search in text[end:end+800]. Ambiguity, main (literal): when a (b) and a (c) candidate overlap each other (e.g. '**Answer:** The answer is 5'), both count. alt_measured: such overlapping (b)/(c) pairs count once, as the (b) span. Could shift the number: (c) candidates like 'is 5' from 'Answer is 5' grade wrong; repeated boxes of the same answer are pooled as separate candidates; the 800-char window may contain the next candidate. If there are no wrong or no right non-final candidates (r_R = 0), the ratio is undefined and the script reports not_computable.

predictions.experiment: Difference-in-differences of re-check rates, RL (T2) minus base (T1), wrong minus right non-final candidates
predictions.recipe: Apply the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1 to s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and to s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue), all 500 rows each, cap hits included. For each file compute r_W and r_R (pooled over rows). Statistic D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)). If a file has zero non-final candidates in a class, that rate is 0.
predictions.note: Files: T2.jsonl (RL) as in k=1 and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/T1.jsonl (base + cue), 500 rows each, cap hits included. Same extraction, grading, non-final filter and flag as k=1 (code identical). r_W, r_R pooled per file; a class with zero non-final candidates gets rate 0 as the recipe says. D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)); refuted iff D > 0.18. alt_measured: overlapping (b)/(c) candidates counted once (as (b)). Both texts start with the stored ' line!' fragment; the text field is used as stored. Base T1 has more cap hits and loops: looping texts repeat boxes/answers many times, so pooled rates are dominated by a few long rows; nothing in the recipe weights rows, so none is applied.

predictions.experiment: Share of final-right answers containing a right non-final candidate followed by a re-check: RL minus base
predictions.recipe: Files: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue). Recompute each row's final score with grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the score_v3 procedure). Keep rows whose final score is right and that are not cap hits (cap_hit false). For each kept row, use the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1. The row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate with the re-check flag set, else 0. F(file) = mean over kept rows. Statistic = F(T2) - F(T1).
predictions.note: Files: T2.jsonl and T1.jsonl as in k=2. Final score recomputed with rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text)['score_v3'] (the score_v3 procedure, not the stored v1/v2 'score'). Kept rows: score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit is False. A kept row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate (k=1 extraction, grading, >= 800 chars after its end) whose 800-char window matches the hold-on regex. F = mean over kept rows per file; statistic F(T2) - F(T1); refuted iff <= 0.0. alt_measured: overlapping (b)/(c) candidates counted once (as (b)); this can only change rows whose sole right flagged candidate is an overlapping (c) line. Note that longer texts have more chances to hold such a candidate, so differences in text length between models feed into the number. If a file had no kept rows the script reports not_computable.
